faqs.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
faqs.q1: How do I know which visa I need?
faqs.a1: It depends on your nationality, destination and purpose of travel. Tell us your trip details and we will point you to the right route.
faqs.q2: Can you guarantee my visa will be approved?
faqs.a2: No. Approval is decided by the destination's authorities. We help you submit a complete, accurate application.
faqs.a3: No. Government fees are paid to the official authority and are separate from any service fee.
faqs.q4: How long does a visa take?
faqs.a4: Processing times vary by destination and season and can change, so apply as early as your destination allows.
faqs.q5: What if I have already been refused?
faqs.a5: We can help you review what happened and prepare a stronger application, but we cannot guarantee a different outcome.

cta.title: Not sure which visa fits?
cta.body: Tell us where you are going and why, and we will map out the documents involved.

meta.title: Tourist Visa Assistance — Visa Expeditor
meta.description: Guided help preparing a tourist visa application: requirements, forms, supporting documents and submission steps.

hero.heading: Tourist Visa Assistance
hero.subhead: Prepare a complete, accurate visitor visa application with step-by-step guidance.

overview.heading: What this service covers
overview.p1: A tourist visa lets you visit a country for leisure, sightseeing or family visits, usually for a limited stay. Requirements vary by destination, nationality and purpose.
overview.p2: We help you confirm what applies to your trip, assemble the right documents and submit a clean application that reflects your travel plans.

whoFor.heading: Who this is for
whoFor.i1: Travelers visiting a country for tourism, holidays or family visits.
whoFor.i2: First-time applicants who want their paperwork checked before submission.
whoFor.i3: Travelers who need a clearer picture of the documents their destination expects.

s1.title: Confirm your requirements
s1.description: Tell us your nationality, destination and travel dates so we can identify the visa route that applies.

s2.title: Prepare your documents
s2.description: We give you a personalized checklist and review each item for completeness and consistency.

s3.title: Complete the forms
s3.description: We help you fill in the application accurately and flag anything that could cause a delay.

s4.title: Submit with confidence
s4.description: You submit through the official channel, with our guidance on fees, appointments and next steps.

r1.label: Passport
r1.value: A valid passport with sufficient remaining validity for your destination.

r2.label: Photo
r2.value: A recent passport-style photograph that meets the destination's specifications.

r3.label: Itinerary
r3.value: Travel dates and, where required, proof of accommodation or onward travel.

r4.label: Supporting documents
r4.value: Evidence of funds, ties to home or purpose of visit, as required by the destination.

faqs.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
faqs.q1: Do I always need a tourist visa?
faqs.a1: No. Many destinations allow visa-free or visa-on-arrival entry for some nationalities. Check your specific passport and destination before assuming you need one.
faqs.q2: How far in advance should I apply?
faqs.a2: Apply as early as your destination allows. Processing times vary and can change seasonally, so leaving extra time is wise.
faqs.a3: No. Approval is always decided by the destination's authorities. We help you submit a complete, accurate application.
faqs.q4: Do you pay the government fee for me?
faqs.a4: No. Government fees are paid to the official authority and are separate from any service fee. We tell you what to expect.
faqs.q5: What if my application is refused?
faqs.a5: We can review what happened and help you understand the options, but we cannot appeal on your behalf or guarantee a different outcome.

cta.title: Planning a trip?
cta.body: Talk to our team and we will map out the documents your destination expects.

meta.title: Business Visa Assistance — Visa Expeditor
meta.description: Prepare a business visa application for meetings, conferences and negotiations with organized company documents.

hero.heading: Business Visa Assistance
hero.subhead: Prepare a professional business travel application for meetings, conferences and negotiations.

overview.heading: What this service covers
overview.p1: A business visa covers short professional visits such as meetings, conferences, negotiations or training. It usually does not permit paid local employment.
overview.p2: We help you present a clear business purpose and the supporting invitation or company documents a consulate may request.

whoFor.heading: Who this is for
whoFor.i1: Professionals travelling for meetings, conferences or negotiations.
whoFor.i2: Employees attending training or corporate events abroad.
whoFor.i3: Business owners visiting partners, suppliers or clients overseas.

s1.title: Confirm the route
s1.description: We check whether your visit qualifies as business travel or needs a different visa category.

s2.title: Gather company documents
s2.description: We help you collect invitation letters, employer confirmations and any event registration.

s3.title: Complete the application
s3.description: We review the forms and supporting documents for consistency with your stated purpose.

s4.title: Submit and get status updates by email
s4.description: You submit through the official channel and we explain what happens next.

r1.label: Passport
r1.value: A valid passport that meets the destination's validity rules.

r2.label: Invitation
r2.value: A letter from the host company or an event organizer, where required.

r3.label: Company documents
r3.value: An employer letter confirming your role, purpose and dates of travel.

r4.label: Proof of funds
r4.value: Evidence that you can cover your stay, if the destination requires it.

faqs.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
faqs.q1: Do I need a business visa for a conference?
faqs.a1: Often yes, though some destinations allow business activities on a visitor visa. Check the rules for your destination and nationality.
faqs.q2: Can I work remotely on a business visa?
faqs.a2: A business visa is normally for meetings and negotiations, not local employment. Remote work rules vary and should be confirmed.
faqs.a3: It is a letter from the company or organization hosting you that states the purpose and dates of your visit.
faqs.q4: Can my employer sponsor the application?
faqs.a4: Your employer can provide supporting documents, but the application is usually submitted by you as the traveller.
faqs.q5: How is a business visa different from a work visa?
faqs.a5: A business visa is for short professional visits. A work visa is for taking up employment and usually requires sponsorship.

cta.title: Travelling for business?
cta.body: Tell us about your trip and we will prepare the documents your destination expects.

meta.title: Student Visa Assistance — Visa Expeditor
meta.description: Organize a student visa application with enrolment, funding and academic documents prepared correctly.

hero.heading: Student Visa Assistance
hero.subhead: Get organized for your study programme with clear document and application guidance.

overview.heading: What this service covers
overview.p1: A student visa allows you to live and study in another country for an approved course. It usually requires proof of enrolment and proof you can support yourself.
overview.p2: We help you assemble the academic, financial and identity documents a student visa application typically requires.

whoFor.heading: Who this is for
whoFor.i1: Students starting a degree, exchange or language programme abroad.
whoFor.i2: Applicants who need to show proof of funds and enrolment.
whoFor.i3: Families preparing a dependant's study move.

s1.title: Confirm the requirements
s1.description: We review your course, destination and nationality to identify the correct student route.

s2.title: Assemble your records
s2.description: We help you gather enrolment, academic and financial documents in the format required.

s3.title: Complete the forms
s3.description: We check the application for consistency with your course and funding.

s4.title: Submit and prepare
s4.description: You submit through the official channel, with guidance on interviews and next steps.

r1.label: Passport
r1.value: A valid passport with the validity your destination requires.

r2.label: Enrolment
r2.value: An offer or enrolment letter from a recognized institution.

r3.label: Proof of funds
r3.value: Evidence you can cover tuition and living costs, as required.

r4.label: Academic records
r4.value: Transcripts, certificates and language test results where required.

faqs.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
faqs.q1: When should I apply for a student visa?
faqs.a1: Once you have your enrolment documents, apply as early as the destination allows, since processing can take time.
faqs.q2: What counts as proof of funds?
faqs.a2: Typically bank statements, sponsorship letters or scholarships showing you can cover your costs. Requirements vary by destination.
faqs.a3: Some destinations allow limited work on a student visa. The rules depend on the country and your course, so confirm before relying on it.
faqs.q4: Can my family come with me?
faqs.a4: Some destinations allow dependants on a student visa and others do not. We can help you check the rules for your case.
faqs.q5: What if my course starts before the visa arrives?
faqs.a5: Contact your institution as soon as you can. Many allow a late start, but the decision is theirs, not ours.

cta.title: Heading abroad to study?
cta.body: Share your programme details and we will build your document checklist.

meta.title: Work Visa Assistance — Visa Expeditor
meta.description: Organize an employment-based visa application with employer and employee documents in order.

hero.heading: Work Visa Assistance
hero.subhead: Organize an employment-based visa application with employer and employee documents in order.

overview.heading: What this service covers
overview.p1: A work visa lets you take up employment in another country, usually tied to a specific employer or role. Requirements depend on the destination's labour rules.
overview.p2: We help coordinate the documents an employer and employee each need so the application is consistent and complete.

whoFor.heading: Who this is for
whoFor.i1: Professionals with a job offer or transfer abroad.
whoFor.i2: Employers relocating staff or hiring internationally.
whoFor.i3: Skilled workers applying through an employer-sponsored route.

s1.title: Confirm the route
s1.description: We check the destination's work visa categories and which one matches your role.

s2.title: Coordinate documents
s2.description: We help the employer and employee prepare sponsorship and qualification documents.

s3.title: Complete the application
s3.description: We review the forms against the role, employer and destination requirements.

s4.title: Submit and plan arrival
s4.description: You submit through the official channel and we explain what to prepare for arrival.

r1.label: Passport
r1.value: A valid passport meeting the destination's validity rules.

r2.label: Job offer
r2.value: A contract or offer letter from the employer.

r3.label: Sponsorship
r3.value: Employer sponsorship or a labour authorization, where the destination requires it.

r4.label: Qualifications
r4.value: Certificates or references proving you meet the role's requirements.

faqs.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
faqs.q1: Do I need a job offer first?
faqs.a1: Most work visas require a confirmed offer or sponsorship before you apply. Some destinations have routes for skilled workers without one.
faqs.q2: Who applies, me or my employer?
faqs.a2: It varies. Often the employer starts the sponsorship and you complete the visa application. We help coordinate both sides.
faqs.a3: Many work visas allow dependants, but the rules differ by destination and role. We can help you check.
faqs.q4: How long does a work visa last?
faqs.a4: It depends on the destination and the role, and may be renewable. Check the specific route for your case.
faqs.a5: Some visas tie you to one employer and others are more flexible. Confirm the conditions before you change jobs.

cta.title: Moving abroad for work?
cta.body: Tell us about the role and destination and we will outline the documents involved.
